He was first and foremost a revolutionary interested in global revolution. He had a mess calling to transform and save the world. But he was accused of being transactional capitalism, and because he was Jewish, it was assumed he was a spy. Stalin had his own issues but benefited from Trotsky's Jewry, slowly amassing power for himself. He also had a background as a police informant, but being a spy for the capitalist was worse. Joseph Stalin won in the end, causing terrible losses to Jewish revolutionaries who were killed.

Leoni and all his children were killed. Transactional capital supported the Bolsheviks and Karl Marx. Marx came from many generations of rabbis, making him a Jewish aristocrat. He was German but moved to England, where he wrote books promoting communism despite being poor. His wealth came from Frederick Engels, a friend whose father was an industrialist. A Jewish capitalist supported Marx because communism benefits transactional capital.

For as soon as the distribution of labor comes into being, each man has a particular exclusive sphere of activity which is forced upon him and from which he cannot escape. He is a hunter, fisherman, herdsman, or critic, and must remain so if he does not want to lose his means of livelihood. In communist society, where nobody has one exclusive sphere of activity but each can become accomplished in any branch they wish, society regulates the general production, making it possible for me to do one thing today and another tomorrow—hunt in the morning, fish in the afternoon, care for cattle in the evening, criticize after dinner without ever becoming a hunter, fisherman, herdsman, or critic.

The problem with capitalism is that it degrades our individuality. We want freedom to enjoy ourselves, but specialization forces us to do one thing according to capitalist needs. In human production, each of us would have affirmed ourselves and our fellow men, objectifying in my production my individuality and its peculiarity, enjoying the activity as an expression of my life. Looking at the product, I see the individual pleasure of realizing that my personality is subjective and visible to the senses, a power raised beyond all doubt.

In using my product, you would have enjoyed realizing by my work, both satisfying a human need and objectifying the human essence, thus fashioning for another human being an object that met his need.
